name: Supplier invoice review
purpose: Teach a supplier invoice review workflow using the uploaded fictional invoice policy, purchase-order XLSX, supplier SQLite snapshot, sample invoice PDF and correspondence template. Match supplier and PO, exactly one SKU or approved alias, quantities after prior approved billing against both orders and deliveries, exact agreed unit price, approved currency and bank, and calculated totals within AZN 0.01. Ask for missing or ambiguous fields. Produce review.xlsx and a conditional correction-letter.docx. Require employee approval and submit one accounting queue record. Keep this fictional demonstration local.

inputs.label: Procedure documents and business inputs
inputs.description: Synthetic PDFs, DOCX, XLSX/CSV records and read-only SQLite reference snapshots.

rules.text: Supplier identifier must correspond to the purchase order and registered bank.
SKU must identify exactly one PO line or approved alias.
Quantity must fit the remaining order and remaining delivery after approved billing.
Unit price must equal the agreed price; AZN only; total difference must be at most AZN 0.01.
Missing, unreadable, conflicting or ambiguous fields require clarification. Supplier and invoice number prevent duplicate accounting submissions.

exceptions: Ask for missing, unreadable or conflicting evidence.
Blocked business findings are completed investigations.
Image-only scans require clarification in the deterministic recipe parser.
approval: Explicit employee approval binds to the exact case revision, structured result, source snapshots and artifact hashes.
assumptions: All supplied company data and credit policies are fictional.
Local simulated queues; no external payments, provisioning or messaging.
Deterministic recipe handles labeled English and Azerbaijani text documents; unrestricted layouts require AI extraction.

# Public process reference for invoice matching

Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-payable/accounts-payable-invoice-matching

Accessed: 2026-10-09. Page last updated: 2025-05-15.

Microsoft describes invoice matching as comparing vendor invoices with purchase orders and receipts. Two-way matching compares price; three-way matching also compares received quantities. Matching discrepancies are checked against company-selected tolerances. Prior invoice lines can matter when partially invoicing an order.

This saved summary establishes a plausible process. The exact AZN tolerance, supplier records, aliases, bank rules and queues in this catalog are fictional demonstration policy. This source does not establish inefficiency at any named company.
assets.templates/letter.txt: Use a clear title, business key, evidence, and specific requested correction. Employee reviewed draft only.
